claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r), input Q=[x]P for the fixed standard secp256k1 generator P, recover x, the deterministic negation-map baby-step/giant-step algorithm in proof.md succeeds with probability at least 1 using at most 2^128.500802 total target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing and verification. Peak memory is at most 2^135.500001 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^127.501176 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is at most 2^0 bytes and is included in memory. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged advice, quantum steps or heuristic assumptions. The exponential memory is required. This is an analytic generic accounting control using the x-coordinate class {R,-R}, not a claim of novelty or practical execution.

experiments.purpose: Exhaustively check signed-window BSGS scalar recovery on a small additive cyclic group, using the class {v,-v} as the analogue of an x-coordinate key. This does not establish production curve behavior, memory bounds, or operation costs.
